sections.h2: Where is the Newaygo County register of deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 1087 Newell Street in White Cloud, in the county's red-roofed Administration Building, with mail going to P.O. Box 885, White Cloud, MI 49349. Phone 231-689-7246, fax 231-689-7271, and the posted hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

White Cloud is the county seat of Newaygo County. The county was created in 1840 and organized in 1851. The register's records for deeds are indexed back to 1910, and the books themselves reach back to 1840, so an old family parcel in this county usually has a paper trail worth pulling before a sale.

The office takes recordable papers about real property: deeds, mortgages, land contracts, trusts and related documents. It does not furnish abstracts, title opinions, forms or notary service, and it cannot tell you when a house was built, because it deals only in land records.

sections.h2: How do I get a document recorded in Newaygo County?
sections.html:
Bring or mail the original, or send it electronically. The county will not record a faxed copy or a photocopy, because only documents with original signatures qualify. Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope so the recorded paper comes back to you promptly.

Recording fees cannot be billed. They are due when the document is recorded, and the office accepts cash, check, debit and credit cards. Card payments carry a service charge of $3.50 on payments up to $100 and 3.5% of the total above that.

Electronic recording follows the Michigan eRecording Standards, which took effect January 1, 2014. The county processes e-filed documents between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and takes payment by ACH. The vendor may add its own charges on top of the county's fees. Four providers are listed: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.

  • Not accepted electronically: court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys.
  • Court documents and death certificates on paper must be certified, because a plain true copy is refused.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded within 20 days of the sale date, and the office asks that you check the sale details with the sheriff's office first.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Newaygo County sale?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. The county tax is $0.55 for each $500 of price or fraction of $500, and the state tax is $3.75 for each $500, so the office's shorthand is $1.10 and $7.50 per $1,000. A sale price rounds up to the next $500 before the rates apply.

The deed must show the total consideration on its face, and any exemption must be written there too, or the office collects both taxes. If you exchange two properties, each deed is taxed on the actual value of the land it conveys. A parcel that lies in two counties needs the price split between them, and tax goes to each county. Documentary stamps are sold only in the county where the land sits. No fee applies to filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, but the deed should say one is attached.

sections.h2: What can the Newaygo County register's records tell me?
sections.html:
Searches are free. Name searches for a grantor or grantee carry no charge, and the office does not run searches for you, though you may use its records yourself. A tract index search works from the legal property description, which you can get from the county equalization department or the local township. A parcel number also works.

Records are public, so a buyer or title agent can pull your deed, any mortgage discharge and any recorded survey. The county does not hold a survey of your lot unless one was recorded, and it knows lot dimensions only for recorded subdivisions and site condominiums. A deed covers the land and not the buildings standing on it.

The register also keeps a fraud alert signup page on the county site, which is worth a look if you own land you do not visit often.

sections.h2: What is the Newaygo County housing picture for sellers?
sections.html:
Newaygo County covers 862 square miles, 813 of them land, in West Michigan. It has more than 230 natural lakes and over 350 miles of rivers and streams, with three large dams, Croton, Hardy and Newaygo, built early in the twentieth century. Hardy Dam is the largest earthen dam east of the Mississippi. Over half the county falls inside the Manistee National Forest, and the county runs parks and the Hardy Dam County Marina.

The Census Bureau counted 49,978 residents in 2020 and estimates 51,622 for July 2025, up 3.3%. Seniors make up 22.7% of the population. The county has 25,455 housing units, and owners occupy 86.5% of homes. The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $186,700, median gross rent was $904, and the median household earned $63,304. Workers spend 30.6 minutes getting to work on average, and the county permitted 111 new buildings in 2025.

Tourism is the county's main economic activity, followed by agriculture and small manufacturing, and the Gerber baby food plant is listed as the largest employer. The Newaygo County Regional Educational Service Agency, based in Fremont, serves the public districts.

Three towns anchor the map. Fremont, a city of 4,516, is home to Gerber and holds the National Baby Food Festival every July. The city of Newaygo, population 2,471, sits on the Muskegon River, which once floated logs to Muskegon mills and now carries canoeists and anglers. White Cloud has 1,479 residents, lies on the White River and has been recognized as a Trail Town on the North Country Trail.

  • Plat books and recorded plats are held by the register, which matters for lake lots in platted subdivisions.
  • A new address comes from the county equalization department, not the register.
  • Confirm the township when you advertise a lake property, since the township assessor sets your tax records.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes and the exemption after I sell in Newaygo County?
sections.html:
The buyer has 45 days to tell the local assessor about the transfer on the state form. The assessor then resets taxable value for the following year to the state equalized value under MCL 211.27a, which is half of true cash value. Residential transfers to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild who does not use the property commercially carry an exception.

A seller who took the principal residence exemption files Form 2602 with the assessor within 90 days of moving out, and the roll drops the exemption on December 31 of that year. The penalty for being late is $5 a day, capped at $200. Ask the Newaygo County treasurer for a tax statement and for the certification the state requires before a warranty deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Newaygo County register of deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., at 1087 Newell Street in White Cloud. E-recorded documents are processed from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on those days.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a $100,000 house in Newaygo County?
faqs.a: It is $860.00: $750.00 to the state and $110.00 to the county. The seller pays it, and prices round up to the next $500 first.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by card?
faqs.a: Yes, by debit or credit card, with a service charge of $3.50 on payments up to $100 and 3.5% on larger ones. Cash and check are accepted too, and fees cannot be billed.

faqs.q: Does Newaygo County accept a sheriff's deed or death certificate by e-recording?
faqs.a: No. Court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys are excluded from e-recording, so they go in on paper with certification where needed.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. Only documents with original signatures are recorded, and a plain true copy of a court document is refused unless the court certified it.
